hints.title: Keypad Jump Representation
hints.text: Map out the allowable moves from each of the 10 digits on a phone pad. Model the number of distinct sequences of length k landing on each digit.

hints.title: Transition Counting by Digit
hints.text: Keep an array of length 10 storing the number of sequences ending at each digit. For each step up to n minus one, update each digit to the sum of sequences from its predecessors.

hints.title: Step-by-Step Modular Accumulation
hints.text: Precompute the jump graph: 0 jumps to [4,6], 1 to [6,8], and so on. Maintain counts for each digit initialized to 1. Repeat n-1 times: for each digit d, update count to the sum of predecessor counts modulo 10^9 + 7. Return the grand sum modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def knightDialer(self, n: int) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        moves = [
            [4, 6],
            [6, 8],
            [7, 9],
            [4, 8],
            [0, 3, 9],
            [],
            [0, 1, 7],
            [2, 6],
            [1, 3],
            [2, 4]
        ]
        dp = [1] * 10
        for _ in range(n - 1):
            next_dp = [0] * 10
            for curr in range(10):
                for nxt in moves[curr]:
                    next_dp[nxt] = (next_dp[nxt] + dp[curr]) % MOD
            dp = next_dp
        return sum(dp) % MOD
```

variables: N: the length of the phone number
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing the state tree with recursion generates up to 3^N paths, leading to exponential time explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since there are only 10 keypad digits, transitioning between steps uses 10 state values in O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize standard DP state transitions and note that digit 5 has no legal outgoing or incoming moves.
complexity.notes: Can also be computed in O(log N) time using 10x10 matrix exponentiation, but linear DP is optimal for N = 5000.

class Solution:
    def knightDialer(self, n: int) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        moves = [
            [4, 6],
            [6, 8],
            [7, 9],
            [4, 8],
            [0, 3, 9],
            [],
            [0, 1, 7],
            [2, 6],
            [1, 3],
            [2, 4]
        ]
        dp = [1] * 10
        for _ in range(n - 1):
            next_dp = [0] * 10
            for curr in range(10):
                for nxt in moves[curr]:
                    next_dp[nxt] = (next_dp[nxt] + dp[curr]) % MOD
            dp = next_dp
        return sum(dp) % MOD
